slides.title: Class Templates Overview
slides.prompt: Class templates allow defining container or utility classes that operate on generic data types. Unlike function templates prior to C++17, class template instantiations historically required explicit type arguments.

slides.title: Class Template Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the syntax to instantiate a Class Template for holding double values.

slides.title: Out-of-Class Member Function Definition
slides.prompt: How must a member function of a class template be defined outside the class body?
options: It must be prefixed with the template header template <typename T> and qualified with ClassName<T>::
It is defined just like a normal non-template class member function
It must use the static keyword prefix
It can only be defined inside header files using inline without template headers
slides.correctAnswer: It must be prefixed with the template header template <typename T> and qualified with ClassName<T>::

slides.title: OutOfClass Definition Qualification
slides.prompt: Fill in the qualification for defining getValue() outside Box<T> class template.

slides.title: Class Template Method Instantiation
slides.prompt: When are member functions of a class template instantiated by the compiler?
options: Only when that specific member function is actually called/used in the code
All member functions are instantiated immediately when the class object is instantiated
At the moment the class template definition is parsed
slides.correctAnswer: Only when that specific member function is actually called/used in the code

slides.title: Default Template Arguments
slides.prompt: Fill in the syntax to specify double as the default type parameter for a class template.

slides.title: Separation of Header and Implementation
slides.prompt: Why are class template definitions usually placed entirely inside header files (.h / .hpp)?
options: The compiler needs access to the full source implementation to generate code whenever the template is instantiated in different translation units
C++ prevents .cpp files from importing template keywords
Including template definitions in .cpp files causes duplicate symbol errors at link time
Template functions are automatically converted to inline macros by the preprocessor
slides.correctAnswer: The compiler needs access to the full source implementation to generate code whenever the template is instantiated in different translation units
